mission: root-cause the 'The product was not found' / storefront 404 report

PLATFORM_AND_API_IDENTIFIED_FROM_CODE.script_responsible_for_storefront_fetch: NONE. No script in this repository fetches the storefront. The storefront is a hosted Gumroad surface at https://aekraft.gumroad.com/, and this factory only ever reads product pages via GET /v2/products/<id>.
PLATFORM_AND_API_IDENTIFIED_FROM_CODE.the_only_storefront_script_found: scripts/shopify_storefront_audit.py targets STORE=https://cpadc7-zh.myshopify.com - a completely different platform (Shopify), unrelated to this error, and it is a read-only audit that performs zero store writes.

ROOT_CAUSE_PROVEN.what_it_actually_is: the response body of GET /v2/products/<id> when <id> is not a valid product identifier
ROOT_CAUSE_PROVEN.how_it_was_triggered: in cycle 122 a diagnostic probe requested GET /v2/products/featured. Gumroad has no such resource; its router answered with a catch-all that treated the literal string 'featured' as a product id and returned success=false plus that message.
IT IS NOT A STOREFRONT FETCH AND NOT A 4: GET https://aekraft.gumroad.com/ returns HTTP 200 right now
the bad-identifier response is HTTP 200 as well - only the body distinguishes them, which is exactly why this kept reading as a storefront fault
no storefront route was ever called by the factory or by that probe
ROOT_CAUSE_PROVEN.classification: WRONG IDENTIFIER - not a missing product, not an unpublished product, not an auth failure, not a permission problem, not a wrong API base

distinction_matrix.product_does_not_exist: NO - fgruzn, iaiyt and uldlwa all resolve and return full records
distinction_matrix.wrong_identifier: YES - the literal string 'featured' was used as a product id

test_design_notes: all tests are offline; no network call is made
the WSHDUE guard excludes test files by design, because a test must quote the forbidden slug in order to forbid it - without that exclusion the guard flags its own docstring
assertions test properties (identical taxonomy sets, body-vs-status discrimination) rather than string-matching docstrings, which produced three brittle failures before being corrected
